check_service_status.description: Check whether ZenQuotes is answering, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Being throttled on the free tier is reported separately from being down, and the answer says whether the connection carries an API key.

mock_response.message: ZenQuotes is up and answering on the free tier.

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

get_on_this_day.description: Get the notable events, births and deaths for a calendar day from ZenQuotes' On This Day feed, each with its year, a plain description and the Wikipedia links behind it. Leave the date empty for today, which is what a daily post wants, or pick any date to look up its anniversaries; the year is ignored. Keep just the categories you need and cap how many of each come back.

parameters.description: The day to look up. Only the month and the day are used, so any year will do. Leave empty for today on the service's clock, US Central time.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: Which of the day's lists to fill in. Leave every box empty for all three. The counts always report the day's totals whichever lists are kept.
parameters.name: categories

parameters.description: How many entries to keep from each list, from 1 to 500. Leave empty for every entry the day holds, which is the default. A busy date can hold a few hundred, so the day's totals are always reported beside the lists.
parameters.name: limit

get_quote_of_the_day.description: Get the one quote ZenQuotes features today, the same for everyone who asks, with the date it is for. A new one is chosen at midnight US Central time, so a daily post scheduled after that never repeats yesterday's; ZenQuotes asks apps to fetch it once a day rather than on every view.

get_quotes.description: Get a batch of random quotes from ZenQuotes, up to 50, optionally all matching one keyword. This is the call the service asks apps to make: it always answers with 50, meant to be kept and looped over locally and refreshed every hour or so, so a workflow that posts several quotes should take them from one batch rather than drawing one at a time.

parameters.description: Only quotes matching this keyword, such as 'happiness'. The dropdown is filled from the service's keyword list, which ZenQuotes serves only to a connection with an API key; on the free tier type the keyword instead. ZenQuotes documents the filter itself beside its subscription too, so a keyless call may be answered with a message asking for a key. Leave empty to draw from every quote.
parameters.name: keyword

parameters.description: Only draw from the custom quotes loaded into the ZenQuotes account the connection's key belongs to. Subscribers can load up to 500 of their own; this needs an API key on the connection. Off by default.
parameters.name: custom

parameters.description: How many quotes to return, from 1 to 50. Defaults to 10. ZenQuotes always sends a batch of 50 and asks apps to reuse it rather than draw one quote at a time, so the batch is trimmed here and its full size is reported as batch_size.
parameters.name: limit

get_quotes_by_author.description: Get a batch of quotes by one author, up to 50, for a themed post or a page about them. The author can be picked from the dropdown, typed as a name or a tag, or chained from List authors. ZenQuotes documents this route beside its subscription, so a keyless connection may be answered with a message asking for a key, which the step reports as it was said.

list_authors.description: List the authors ZenQuotes holds quotes by, each with the tag the author actions take and a link to their quotes, so a step can choose one here and hand the tag on. The service adds figures every month, so the list is fetched live rather than written down. ZenQuotes serves this list only to a connection with an API key; on the free tier the step reports the service's own message asking for one. Turn on custom to list the authors of the account's own custom quotes instead.
list_authors.name: list_authors

parameters.description: List only the authors of the custom quotes loaded into the ZenQuotes account the connection's key belongs to. Needs an API key on the connection. Off by default.
parameters.name: custom

list_keywords.description: List the keywords ZenQuotes can filter quotes by, such as happiness, so a step can choose one here and hand it to Get quotes or Get a random quote. The list is the service's own and is fetched live. ZenQuotes serves it only to a connection with an API key; on the free tier the step reports the service's own message asking for one.
list_keywords.name: list_keywords

description: Pull inspirational quotes from ZenQuotes, the hand-curated quotation API. Get the quote of the day, draw one at random or a batch to reuse, narrow to an author such as Abraham Lincoln or a keyword such as happiness, list the authors and keywords the service knows, and read the notable events, births and deaths for any day of the year from its On This Day feed. Works without a key on the free tier, which allows 5 requests every 30 seconds; add a ZenQuotes API key to lift the limit and unlock the subscriber options.
